## Not Every Hero Wears A Cape

rows.start: After the day, look at what actually happened. If you did th

beside.label: Draft c1
beside.text: After the day, look at what actually happened. If you did the Protector action(s), not feeling better right away is information to learn from. Healing is nonlinear, and sometimes standing up for yourself might make you feel worse at first. Not doing it is harder to figure out. Fear is the first guess, but maybe you didn't know how or why. Or you were just worn out, or whoever said they'd help couldn't make it. 🤗

beside.text: Sometimes a session goes great, and a few days later you're skipping lunch and saying yes to everything again. I wouldn't try going deeper next time. I'd guess you just haven't brought any of it out with you yet. Whatever you did for your little one in there, try a tiny bit of it out here, like texting a friend that you're having a rough day instead of saying you're fine.

headings: # Altered States Can Deepen the Therapy

rows.label: 101.1: 97.8 as it is, beside draft d4 (100% AI; not in)
rows.start: Milder reactions afterward count as caution signs too, like

beside.label: Draft d4
beside.text: I'd count the milder stuff too, like coming back from trip after trip confused or spaced out. If it gets bad, or it keeps happening when you're sober, I wouldn't wait to see a psychiatrist about it. And if you think a medicine you're on is part of the problem, ask your doctor before you stop. Some, like benzos, can be dangerous to quit all at once. Alcohol too, once your body depends on it.

beside.label: Before: P10 ended with it
beside.text: With that under you, belonging with people can get a lot less desperate. Not all at once, but the Guide keeps watching for the moment your little one starts thinking, "If they stop liking me, I won't belong anywhere," and keeps reminding it that a group's approval isn't the deepest belonging there is. By the way, this job doesn't have to be called the Guide. The Wise One works, or your Inner Teacher, and "Guru" does for some people.

rows.label: 100.2 A: treats and pampering at set times
rows.start: Maybe you've let a small child win at Go Fish and never foun

beside.label: Before
beside.text: Maybe you've let a small child win at Go Fish and never found a good time to start playing for real. Who wants to be the grown-up who finally wins? Without the Guide, you can slide from looking after your little one into spoiling it the same way. Sweets and screens can pass for loving yourself, and so can getting it out of anything hard. Comfort does better at set times, where it can't get out of hand. It shouldn't get canceled as a punishment after a bad day, either (ST-CA, section 17.1.4).

rows.label: 100.1 A: your heading and P9, word for word
rows.start: The Guide also points beyond itself, toward

beside.label: Before (under "A Belonging Deeper Than Any Group")
beside.text: The Guide also points beyond itself, toward a belonging deeper than any group, one that doesn't ask you to give up being yourself. That might be nature, or existence itself. It might be whatever your tradition sees as ultimate. Love can come from any of these places, and you also belong there, which is a little different. Maybe you've felt that outside somewhere, like you didn't need anybody's okay to be there. The way in is time in nature and contemplative practice, like meditation.
